extraction.name: Vibravox: A Dataset of French Speech Captured with Body-conduction Audio Sensors
extraction.description: Vibravox is a dataset compliant with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) containing audio recordings using five different body-conduction audio sensors.
extraction.creator: Julien Hauret, Malo Olivier, Thomas Joubaud, Christophe Langrenne, Sarah Poirée, Véronique Zimpfer, and Éric Bavu
extraction.citeAs: Hauret, J., Olivier, M., Joubaud, T., Langrenne, C., Poirée, S., Zimpfer, V., & Bavu, É. (2025). Vibravox: A Dataset of French Speech Captured with Body-conduction Audio Sensors. Speech Communication.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The Vibravox dataset was developed through a rigorous data collection process. A total of 200 participants contributed to the dataset, with 188 retained after post-processing to ensure high-quality data.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Some audio clips had various shortcomings: mispronounced sentences, sensors shifting from their initial positions, occasional sensor malfunctions, or instances where a microphone was inadvertently left unequipped.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The dataset contains audio data from an airborne microphone used as a reference and five different body-conduction audio sensors: two in-ear microphones, two bone conduction vibration pickups, and a laryngophone.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The exact timeframe is not specified, but it was conducted over a period allowing 200 participants to contribute.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Post-filtering techniques were applied to enhance data quality and facilitate interpretability.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: A series of three automatic filters were applied to remove utterances with obvious deficiencies.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The preprocessing steps included computing indicators for evaluating audio capture quality, such as Phoneme Error Rate (PER), sound levels during voiced and non-voiced segments, and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations about the recording conditions and linguistic transcriptions are included in the corpus.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: The annotations were created using a custom setup and software developed for the recording user interface.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The annotations were analyzed to ensure high-quality labels for the speech-to-phonemes task.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Each utterance was annotated with correct pronunciation and a sufficiently high SNR.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: The participants were 188 adults (97 female, 91 male) with ages ranging from 18 to 82 years old.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: The whisper-timestamped model was used for annotating audio samples.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly available on HuggingFace and will be updated with versioning information.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains sensitive human attributes such as age, gender, and possibly biometric information like heart rate and breathing.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset has the potential to improve communication in noisy environments and advance research in body-conducted speech analysis.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset addresses several limitations found in existing datasets, such as limited diversity of audio sensors and lack of noise recordings.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has some limitations, including the non-negligible amount of data excluded during post-processing.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset can be used for speech enhancement, speech-to-phonemes recognition, and speaker verification tasks.
